childhood.title: Childhood
childhood.description: Grew up in India with an early fascination for computers and games. Taking things apart, tinkering with software, and wondering how it all worked turned into a habit that eventually became a career.

school.title: School
school.description: School years built the foundation: mathematics, science, and the first lines of code. The plan that stuck was simple — study computer science and keep building things on the side.

college.title: Vellore Institute of Technology
college.description: B.Tech in Computer Science & Engineering at VIT Vellore. Graduated as a merit holder with a GPA of 8.6/10, with coursework in advanced algorithms, distributed systems, operating systems, networks and DBMS.

firstJob.title: Software Engineer 1 · Bank of America
firstJob.description: Built low-latency C++ and Python services for the Apex/Martini Global Repo Trading Platform. Designed Optimus, a Python/Tornado support automation platform with RASA NLU, and a React + Flask regression framework that cut manual QA effort by roughly 90%. Earned the 2x Global Gold Recognition Award.

current.title: Software Engineer 2 · PayU
current.description: Leading PRISM 2.0, a secure multi-tenant financial intelligence platform for large-scale SMS ingestion and analysis, along with an AA TSP consent platform. Focused on distributed, event-driven systems, cloud-native delivery, observability and reliability.

skills.title: Skills & Technologies
skills.description: Backend and full-stack engineer with a broad toolkit — from low-latency C++ services and Python APIs to React front ends and cloud-native delivery on AWS.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Pricing intelligence, NLP-driven news analysis, LLM task planning and full-stack platforms. Most of it is open source on GitHub — PricePilot and NewsMelt are good places to start.

future.title: What's Next
future.description: Going deeper into LLM agents and RAG pipelines, system design at scale, and a bit of Rust. Currently re-reading Designing Data-Intensive Applications — again, because it is that good.
